Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

I’m sorry phrase

also sorry, I regret it, regret, apologise, feel really bad about, feel bad about, you’ll be sorry, you’ll regret it, you’ll feel bad, I’m sorry to hear that, heartache

classical

Traupman 157, 383

mē paenitet

I’m sorry, I regret it

+ gen. or infinitive.

Other words

  • doleō, dolēre, doluī — be sorry about, grieve over

    verb, second conjugation; with the accusative and infinitive, or dē with the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 330: doleō mē in vītam paulō sērius tamquam in viam ingressum (Lewis & Short), s.v. sērus; Traupman 98: valdē dolēre dē (+ abl.); Traupman 22: Traupman’s mē paenitet haec cognōscere for “I’m sorry to hear that” uses the verb of regret for one’s own doing (Lewis & Short: “to repent, regret”); for sympathy, doleō; Traupman 314

    Sorrow for what has happened, not an apology: mē paenitet is “I regret what I did”.

  • cordolium, cordoliī n. — heartache: tibi cordolium erit, you’ll be sorry

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Cist. 1.1.67; Plaut. Poen. 1.2.86 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 98: tibi cordolium erit; Traupman 153

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.; in ōrātiōne solūtā rāra)

    Lewis & Short: “sorrow at heart, grief (ante- and post-class.)”.

  • paenitentia, paenitentiae f. — regret, repentance

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 157

    Lewis & Short: not in Cicero; the everyday construction is mē paenitet.

Examples

  • Sī quid perperam fēcī, mē paenitet.

    If I’ve done anything wrong, I’m sorry (an apology for a child)Traupman 112

See also excuse me, I apologise, I’m ashamed.
